items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: There’s nothing – it’s not Jimmy Giuffre. It’s not Chet Baker.

ctx.x: Garbarek is the best curved soprano player ever.

Yeah, he’s great, and he has – because he has found his own sound. Also, he has a very bold, declaratory, emphatic way of playing, stylistically, that fits his tone. There’s nothing – it’s not Jimmy Giuffre. It’s not Chet Baker. There is nothing mysterious about it. That guy lays it down, like that, as coming from that part of the world, that’s the way they play. They’re very stark. It’s stark. It’s the way that landscape is up there, and that’s why it fits with him. But I’m not sure anybody else could get away…

about a straight horn and the airstream. The airstream is direct, and you get the effect very quickly. Trumpet’s like this. Boom, it’s out. Soprano, it’s out there. Tenor, and alto to a lesser extent – we’re talking milliseconds here, I guess. I scientifically can’t tell you, but it appears to me to be something about the flow of the airstream, the immediacy of a straight horn compared to a curved horn, that is an attraction.
